documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o F here to establish care. Teaches kindergarten. Switching from her old PCP, last physical about 2 yrs ago with her old PCP.

PMH: alpha-thalassemia trait, told during her pregnancy in 2019. No other medical problems. Never told of a heart murmur.
OB: G1P1, term vaginal delivery 2019, no complications.
PSH: none other.
Meds: prenatal vitamin daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, started by her OB and she kept taking them; may want another child at some point.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother has rheumatic heart disease. Alpha-thal trait in her immediate family. Mother's pregnancies were all fine.
SH: lives with partner and their 2 y/o. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Both she and partner were born outside the US.

ROS: negative, no dyspnea, palpitations, edema, heavy menses.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as recorded. HEENT nl, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, S1 S2 normal, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abd soft NT. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. Ext warm without edema. Skin no rashes.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap today. CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, iron studies to sort out trait vs iron. HIV and hep C once, she agreed. PHQ-2 0.
2. Alpha-thal trait: expect mild microcytosis, ferritin to make sure no iron deficiency on top. Continue folic acid, I'll take over the Rx.
3. Records: release signed for old PCP and OB, want the 2019 hemoglobin workup.
4. Flu this fall. COVID primary series done in the spring per her card.
RTC 1 yr or sooner.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Maricel, your labs are back. Blood counts show the small red cells we expected from the thalassemia trait, and your iron level is normal, so there is no iron deficiency to treat. Kidney, liver, thyroid and cholesterol are all fine. HIV and hepatitis C negative. The Pap result usually takes another week. Keep taking the folic acid.

Alpha-globin gene analysis: two-gene deletion on one chromosome, consistent with alpha-thalassemia trait. Spontaneous vaginal delivery at 39 weeks, 2019, uncomplicated. Postpartum visit normal. Tdap given 3/2019 at 30 weeks.

Prior primary care: 2018 Pap normal. MMR x2 in childhood per school record. COVID vaccine x2 spring 2021 (pharmacy card). Allergies: none known. Medications: prenatal vitamin, folic acid 1 mg daily.

PCP review: trait confirmed by gene testing, nothing else new. Partner's testing not in these records.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 04/01/2023
Patient: Maricel Srisai, 28 F
Allergies: NKDA

CC: shortness of breath and racing heart

HPI: 28 year old woman with alpha thalassemia trait, otherwise healthy, two days of breathlessness that has been getting worse, now cannot lie flat and has been sleeping propped on pillows, with a fluttering, fast heartbeat on and off. No chest pain, no fever, no leg swelling, no recent travel. Not pregnant per patient, urine hCG negative.

PMH: alpha-thal trait. Prior SVD. Meds: prenatal vitamin, folic acid 1 mg. SH: never smoker, no EtOH, kindergarten teacher. FH: mother with rheumatic heart disease.

Exam: in mild respiratory distress, speaking full sentences. BP 110/70, HR 120 and irregularly irregular, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA, afebrile. Cardiac: irregular rhythm; low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur loudest at the apex with an opening snap. Lungs: crackles at both bases. JVP difficult to assess. Extremities without edema.

ECG: atrial fibrillation, rate ~120, no ST or T changes.
CXR: venous congestion, enlarged LA.
Labs: hs troponin 3, BMP normal, CBC with microcytosis consistent with known trait.

ED course: metoprolol 5 mg IV x2 with rate improvement, furosemide 20 mg IV with good urine output and easier breathing. Spontaneously converted to sinus rhythm at about 21:30. Ambulated on room air, SpO2 97%.

Impression: new atrial fibrillation with rapid rate and pulmonary congestion; exam and film most consistent with rheumatic mitral stenosis, given family history.

Disposition: discharged home in sinus rhythm 23:40. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily. Furosemide 20 mg daily for 5 days. Needs echocardiogram and cardiology; follow up with PCP within one week. Return for chest pain, worsening breathing or recurrent palpitations.

[Received by fax 4/19/2023 after records request.]

documents.title: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello doctor, I went to the emergency room yesterday because I couldn't breathe lying down and my heart was racing. They said my heart was out of rhythm and that I may have a problem with a heart valve, like my mom. They gave me two new pills, metoprolol and a water pill for 5 days. I feel much better today. They told me to see you this week and to get a heart ultrasound. What should I do?

documents.title: RE: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you are feeling better. Keep taking both pills as they told you. The office will call tomorrow to get you in this week, I have Thursday morning open. If the racing or breathlessness comes back before then, go back to the ER.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 72. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. Normal axis. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

Sent home on metoprolol succinate 25 daily and 5 days of furosemide, which she finished yesterday. Since then breathing back to normal, sleeping flat, no palpitations. Mild fatigue first two days on metoprolol, better now. ED told her they suspect a mitral valve problem like her mother's. We do not have the ED record yet, front desk requesting.

O: vitals as charted, regular pulse. Appears well. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, soft low-pitched diastolic rumble at the apex in left lateral position, which I did not hear at her last physical. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG in office: sinus rhythm 72, normal intervals.

A/P
1. Paroxysmal AF, single episode, now sinus on metoprolol. Check TSH, BMP after diuretic.
2. Probable rheumatic mitral stenosis given exam and her mother's history. Needs TTE and cardiology; referral placed today, asked for a visit within a month.
3. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
Return precautions reviewed. Will call with labs.

events.reason: suspected rheumatic mitral stenosis, atrial fibrillation

reports.text: Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness with normal systolic function, LVEF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Mitral valve: rheumatic morphology with commissural fusion and diastolic doming of the anterior leaflet. Mitral valve area 1.6 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 6 mmHg at heart rate 68. Mild mitral regurgitation. Left atrium enlarged, volume index 46 mL/m2. No left atrial thrombus seen on transthoracic imaging. Aortic valve trileaflet, opens normally, no aortic regurgitation. Tricuspid valve normal with trace regurgitation; estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 36 mmHg. Inferior vena cava normal in size with normal collapse. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Rheumatic mitral stenosis, MVA 1.6 cm2, mean gradient 6 mmHg; mild MR; enlarged left atrium; normal LV function; PASP 36 mmHg.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient Cardiology Consultation
Date of visit: 05/18/2023
Referred by: primary care, for mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Srisai, a 28 year old kindergarten teacher with alpha-thalassemia trait, seen in the emergency department on 4/1 with AF and rapid rates and pulmonary congestion that settled with rate control and diuresis, converting to sinus rhythm. She has felt well since, with no palpitations, orthopnea or exertional limitation. She takes metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, a prenatal vitamin and folic acid. No known drug allergies. Her mother has rheumatic heart disease. She recalls no childhood rheumatic fever. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BP and HR as recorded, regular rhythm. Loud S1, opening snap, and a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble at the apex. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today: rheumatic mitral valve, MVA 1.6 cm2 by planimetry, mean gradient 6 mmHg at HR 68, mild MR, LA volume index 46 mL/m2, LVEF 60%, PASP 36 mmHg.

Assessment: progressive (stage B) rheumatic mitral stenosis. Her decompensation occurred with AF and fast rates, which shorten diastolic filling. Currently in sinus rhythm.

Recommendations:
1. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
2. Repeat echocardiogram yearly, sooner with symptoms.
3. She mentions she may want a second child. Please have her see us before trying to conceive; pregnancy increases the gradient and needs close follow-up.
4. Seek care promptly for palpitations or breathlessness.
We will see her in 1 year with an echo.

Outside cardiology group

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit, 28 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics and Gynecology, prenatal visit
Date of visit: 12/03/2025
cc: primary care physician

31 y/o G2P1 at 27w5d by early ultrasound, with rheumatic mitral stenosis and alpha-thalassemia trait, here for her routine third-trimester visit. She feels well, no complaints, no recent illness, no trauma. Glucose screening normal, no maternal diabetes. Antibody screen negative; no alloimmunization.

Labs: Toxoplasma, CMV and parvovirus B19 serologies negative. Cell-free DNA screening earlier in pregnancy low risk, no chromosomal abnormality.

Ultrasound today: fetal ascites, bilateral fetal pleural effusions and a small pericardial effusion. Amniotic fluid normal. Growth appropriate.

Assessment/Plan:
- Fetal effusions as above, infectious and immune causes not supported by the workup to date. With maternal alpha-thalassemia trait, fetal alpha-thalassemia is a leading concern. Problem list: alpha-thalassemia.
- Neonatology consulted today.
- Maternal peripheral blood smear sent.
- Maternal-fetal medicine to follow closely.
- Medications: prenatal vitamin, folic acid 1 mg. NKDA.

Discussed findings with patient and partner at length.

documents.title: Patient call after ultrasound

documents.body: Pt called crying, says her scan Wednesday showed fluid around the baby and the OB thinks it may be the thalassemia. Wants to talk to her doctor. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP callback
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called back, spoke 20 min. We have not received the OB note yet. She explained the ultrasound findings as she understands them, and that the OB, the high-risk pregnancy team and the newborn doctors are all involved. Listened, answered what I could, encouraged her to write down questions for the specialists. She feels well herself, no breathlessness or palpitations. She has support from her partner. Will watch for the OB letter. Told her she can message any time.

Obstetrics and Gynecology, prenatal visit
Date of visit: 01/05/2026

31 y/o G2P1 at 32w3d, rheumatic mitral stenosis, alpha-thalassemia trait, followed since the 28-week visit. New concern: about two months of burning and pins-and-needles along the outer right thigh. Worse when she stands for a long time at work, eases when she lies down. No injury. No back pain, no weakness. Weight up 25 lb this pregnancy.

Exam: right thigh skin normal, no redness or swelling. Patch of reduced light-touch sensation over the anterolateral thigh. Hip exam normal, full painless range. Lumbar spine nontender, normal motion. Patellar and ankle reflexes intact and symmetric. Straight leg raise negative right and left. Strength normal.

Assessment: meralgia paresthetica, right, lateral femoral cutaneous nerve compression, typical in late pregnancy.
Plan: reassurance, avoid tight waistbands and belts, change position and sit when possible during the school day. Expect improvement after delivery. Return if weakness or bladder or bowel changes.
Meds: prenatal vitamin, folic acid 1 mg. NKDA.

[Received with delivery records 3/6/2026.]

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 01/16/2026
Patient: Maricel Srisai, 31 F, G2P1 at 34w0d
Allergies: NKDA

CC: left leg swelling

HPI: 31 year old pregnant woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis and alpha-thal trait. Three days of left leg swelling with a tight, aching feeling, worse the longer she stands, now hard to walk on. No injury, no long trips. No chest pain, no shortness of breath. Fetal movement normal.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, folic acid. SH: no tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable and within normal limits. Left calf visibly larger than right and tender, faint redness, skin intact without breakdown or ulcers. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses intact both feet. Lungs clear. Gravid abdomen, nontender.

Ultrasound: left popliteal vein will not compress, consistent with DVT.
Labs: CBC with platelets normal, Hgb at her usual low level, creatinine normal, PT/INR normal.

Impression: acute left lower extremity DVT (popliteal) in the third trimester.

Plan: discussed with on-call OB. Enoxaparin 70 mg subcutaneous every 12 hours (1 mg/kg, weight 69 kg), first dose given here at 21:00, teaching done. Prescription sent. OB follow-up early next week; PCP follow-up. Leg elevation, walking as tolerated. Return for chest pain, breathlessness, bleeding, or decreased fetal movement.

[Received 1/23/2026.]

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 02/20/2026   Discharged: 02/24/2026
Patient: Maricel Srisai, 31 y/o, G2P1 -> P2
Allergies: NKDA

Admission diagnosis: decreased fetal movement at 39w0d with nonreassuring fetal testing.
Discharge diagnoses: Category III fetal heart rate tracing, resolved with resuscitation; arrest of active phase of labor; low transverse cesarean delivery; left popliteal DVT in pregnancy on enoxaparin; rheumatic mitral stenosis; alpha-thalassemia trait.

Prenatal course: rheumatic mitral stenosis and alpha-thalassemia trait. Fetal ascites, pleural and pericardial effusions on the 28-week ultrasound, followed by maternal-fetal medicine and neonatology; maternal smear from that visit showed microcytic, hypochromic red cells with target cells, consistent with alpha-thalassemia trait. Right meralgia paresthetica. Left popliteal DVT 1/16/2026 on therapeutic enoxaparin. ED visit 2/13 for decreased fetal movement, reassuring.

Hospital course: presented to triage 2/20 with six hours of decreased movement. BP 120/75, P 80, T 36.8 C. Fetal tracing with minimal variability, no accelerations and recurrent late decelerations, Category III. Ultrasound with oligohydramnios, BPP 4/10. Admitted to labor and delivery. Last enoxaparin dose 2/20 at 07:00 at home, held from admission. Intrauterine resuscitation with left lateral positioning and IV fluid bolus; tracing returned to Category I within the hour. Induction of labor begun with close monitoring.
Early 2/21 membranes ruptured, clear fluid, followed by regular contractions every 3 minutes. Cervix 6 cm, 90% effaced, -2 station. After five hours of adequate contractions she was in severe pain and requested analgesia; epidural placed at 10:15, more than 24 hours after her last therapeutic dose. Repeat exam unchanged in dilation, effacement and station. Intrauterine pressure catheter averaging 220 MVU per 10 minutes. Afebrile, no signs of chorioamnionitis. Fetal tracing reassuring throughout labor.
Diagnosis of active-phase arrest; low transverse cesarean delivery under epidural anesthesia 2/21 at 15:40, uncomplicated. Liveborn infant handed to the neonatal team.
Postpartum: recovered well, ambulating, tolerating diet. Enoxaparin restarted 24 hours after surgery at 60 mg every 12 hours (weight 63 kg). Postop day 1 Hgb 10.2. Mitral stenosis: no dyspnea, no arrhythmia on telemetry during labor.

Discharge medications: enoxaparin 60 mg subcut every 12 hours until 4/17/2026 (at least 6 weeks postpartum and 3 months total), acetaminophen 1000 mg every 6 hours as needed, prenatal vitamin daily, folic acid 1 mg daily.
Follow-up: OB incision check in 1 to 2 weeks; postpartum visit 6 weeks; PCP; cardiology.

[Received by fax 3/6/2026 after request.]

documents.title: Baby is here
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doctor, I wanted you to know I had the baby last Saturday by C-section. The baby was not moving much so they kept me, then my labor stopped at 6 cm. The baby is with the newborn team. I am home now, still on the blood thinner shots, now 60 twice a day until April 17. I will make an appointment after my OB checkup.

documents.title: RE: Baby is here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, I have been thinking of you. Rest as much as you can. Keep up the shots until April 17. Call right away for chest pain, trouble breathing, heavy bleeding or a hot, red incision. We'll request the hospital records and see you in April.

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 8 weeks after cesarean on 2/21 for arrest of labor. Records from the hospital and OB arrived 3/6 and are reviewed. Did her last enoxaparin injection 4/17 as planned, no bleeding problems. Left leg back to normal size, no pain. OB postpartum check went fine, incision healed. Right outer thigh tingling much better since delivery, only notices it after a long day. Sleeping in pieces with the baby, partner helping. Mood mostly OK, tired. No breathlessness, orthopnea or palpitations. Still has not seen cardiology; appointment now booked for May.
Meds: prenatal vitamin, folic acid. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted, regular pulse. Well appearing. Heart regular, apical diastolic rumble as before. Lungs clear. Abdomen: low transverse incision well healed. Legs: symmetric, no edema, no calf tenderness. Right thigh: small area of slightly reduced light touch anterolaterally, strength and reflexes normal.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
1. Left popliteal DVT in pregnancy, provoked, completed 3 months of enoxaparin. Stopped. Moved to history.
2. Meralgia paresthetica, right, from OB note 1/5, improving postpartum. Added to list. Expect it to settle.
3. Pregnancy items resolved on the problem list.
4. Rheumatic MS: cardiology 5/19, glad it is booked.
5. Alpha-thal trait, post-cesarean: CBC and iron today.
6. Mood: PHQ-9 4, normal postpartum fatigue, she knows to reach out.
Physical in the summer.

documents.title: Blood count and iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count is nearly back to your usual level and iron stores are normal, so no iron pills needed. Keep the prenatal vitamin and folic acid.

reports.text: Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness, LVEF 60%, no regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal size and function. Mitral valve rheumatic with commissural fusion and anterior leaflet doming. Mitral valve area 1.6 cm2 by planimetry. Mean gradient 6 mmHg at heart rate 70. Mild mitral regurgitation. Left atrium enlarged, volume index 47 mL/m2. Aortic valve normal. Trace tricuspid regurgitation, estimated PASP 34 mmHg. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Rheumatic mitral stenosis, MVA 1.6 cm2, mean gradient 6 mmHg, unchanged from 2023; mild MR; LVEF 60%.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 70. Normal intervals and axis. No ST or T-wave abnormality.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient Cardiology Follow-up
Date of visit: 05/19/2026

Ms. Srisai returns, last seen by us 6/2024. Since then she stopped metoprolol on her own in late 2024, conceived in May 2025, and delivered by cesarean on 2/21/2026 for arrest of labor after a pregnancy complicated by fetal effusions and a left popliteal DVT treated with enoxaparin through 4/17. She was not seen here during the pregnancy. She reports no palpitations, orthopnea, or exertional dyspnea, including during labor. Meds: prenatal vitamin, folic acid 1 mg. NKDA.

Exam: regular rhythm, loud S1, opening snap, apical diastolic rumble. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: sinus rhythm 70.
Echo: MVA 1.6 cm2, mean gradient 6 mmHg at HR 70, LA volume index 47 mL/m2, PASP 34 mmHg, LVEF 60%, mild MR. Unchanged from 2023.

Assessment: stable stage B rheumatic mitral stenosis in sinus rhythm, asymptomatic.
Plan: echo and visit yearly. Please let us know early in any future pregnancy. Prompt evaluation for palpitations or breathlessness.

Outside cardiology group

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32 y/o here for annual, five months after her cesarean. Feels like herself again, sleeping better. Thigh tingling gone for about a month. Saw cardiology 5/19, echo unchanged, yearly follow-up; letter received. No palpitations, dyspnea, orthopnea, leg swelling or calf pain. Off enoxaparin since April. Taking prenatal vitamin and folic acid. Back to school in the fall.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, apical diastolic rumble, unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, incision healed. Legs symmetric, no edema. Right thigh sensation normal today. Mood bright.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Rheumatic MS stage B, sinus rhythm, cardiology yearly.
2. Hx paroxysmal AF 2023, no recurrence.
3. Hx provoked DVT in pregnancy, off anticoagulation.
4. Meralgia paresthetica resolved.
5. Alpha-thal trait: CBC; continue folic acid.
6. Health maintenance: CMP, lipids, TSH. Pap due 2027. Flu and COVID this fall, booked in November.
RTC November.
